name: Amsterdam
summary: Book the Anne Frank House and Van Gogh Museum well ahead, then fill the gaps with canal walks and the Jordaan. Everything central is within a 30-minute walk or a short tram.
seasonNote: Tulip season runs mid-March to early May; summer is busiest and winter is dark and damp.
arrival: Trains from Schiphol reach Centraal in 15 to 20 minutes.
gettingAround: Walk or take trams; watch for bike lanes before stepping off a kerb.
cashTip: Many places are card-only; some do not take credit cards, so carry a debit card too.
foodTip: Try a fresh stroopwafel, herring from a stall, bitterballen with beer and Indonesian rijsttafel.
buyTip: Aged Gouda, stroopwafels and Delft-style ceramics from reputable shops.
baseArea: Jordaan, the canal ring or De Pijp

connections.note: Direct Eurostar high-speed trains; book ahead.
Direct trains several times a day.

items.name: Rijksmuseum
items.summary: The national museum, home to Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer's Milkmaid.
items.expect: Timed entry and crowds in the Gallery of Honour.
items.tip: Book the first slot and go straight to the second floor.

whyVisit: The national museum, home to Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer's Milkmaid.

items.name: Canal Ring and Jordaan
items.summary: The 17th-century ring of canals, gabled houses and bridges, with the Jordaan's lanes beside it.
items.expect: Bikes everywhere; boats fill up on sunny days.
items.tip: Walk the Nine Streets, then take a small open-boat cruise near dusk.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.
items.sourceNote: Editorial selection. Durations, spending allowances and itinerary advice are planning estimates; check opening days and prices with the venue before you go.
whyVisit: The 17th-century ring of canals, gabled houses and bridges, with the Jordaan's lanes beside it.
The planned canal belt is a World Heritage site and the city's defining sight.
visitFlow: Walk Prinsengracht and the Nine Streets.
Take a one-hour canal cruise.
items.bestFor: Visitors interested in architecture and design and history and context
tradeoffs: Bikes everywhere; boats fill up on sunny days.
Walk the Nine Streets, then take a small open-boat cruise near dusk.
